lines.text: Do you know how earthquakes work? The ground under you is slowly bending, until it suddenly snaps.
Earth's plates grind past each other along cracks called faults. But friction locks the edges together.
The plates keep moving, a few centimeters a year, so the rock bends and stores energy, for decades or even centuries.
When the stress beats the friction, the fault slips in seconds, and all that stored energy is released at once.
It spreads as seismic waves. Fast P waves squeeze the rock and arrive first. Slower S waves shake it side to side, and do more damage.
Each step up the magnitude scale releases about thirty two times more energy. A magnitude seven releases about a thousand times more than a five.
Because P waves arrive first, sensors can send alerts seconds before the strong shaking. Seconds that are enough to take cover.
So every earthquake is rock, letting go.
